name: Dora Frost
life: “I still remember sketching a face in the blur on the laundry window.” Monday often includes a stop at the market by Market Flats, where Dora often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I draw the people who wait for their washing and forget what their own faces are doing.
appearance: Dora has a blunt cut just below the ears, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a dark green knitted vest. It usually goes with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. When somebody else has the floor, Dora listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Dora talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Dora's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To rent a small studio while retaining control of the portraits.
family: Katherine Nielsen is Dora’s cousin. Dora chooses the music. Katherine puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The first straight paycheck*, Katherine says, “I found the wage slip on the pavement. I knew what it might cost him if the wrong friend saw it.”
connections: Joanna Zhou. Artist and sitter discuss what making a likeness entitles anyone else to see. Also in the story is Lucia Byrd (partner).

reactions.situation: A portrait sitter asks for the drawing back
reactions.response: Dora asks the sitter whether the drawing can be stored privately or should go home with them.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Dora accepts a small agreed amount if paying lets the neighbor keep their pride.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Dora says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
